editorial.headline: Nationally Open, Blocked in Bali: Recreation at a Regulatory Divide
editorial.standfirst: This broad entertainment-and-recreation activity permits full foreign ownership nationally, yet Bali blocks its PMA registration under a permanent moratorium tied to its recorded risk class.
editorial.body:
KBLI 93299 is a deliberately wide berth for entertainment and recreation operations. It includes the operation of ski hills and fairgrounds, recreation-equipment hire inseparable from a facility, and the production of live entertainment or recreation shows outside sport and art. Its scope also reaches independent animators within facilities, computer-game rooms, self-service amusements, airsoft and paintball fields, virtual-reality and geolocation experiences, billiard and bowling venues, escape rooms, laser games, light-and-sound shows, underwater-tour guiding, and fireworks making and displays.

The common thread is operation: running, staging, supplying or managing the experience. That can include mechanical rides and shows run by independent providers at exhibitions, folk festivals and Christmas markets, as well as picnic grounds unrelated to nature conservation. It also covers the technical planning, provision, arrangement and operation of audiovisual and special-effects equipment connected with managing live entertainment and recreation. The activity is open at Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, giving the category room to accommodate both contained venues and larger operational formats.

Nationally, the record is clear: the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A founder considering the activity at national level can therefore read the foreign-investment position as fully open. But that ceiling is not a portable answer for Bali. National foreign ownership and the provincial registration result are separate facts in the record; confusing them would overlook the constraint that governs a Bali PMA filing.

In Bali today, a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA. At Besar scale, OSS risk is recorded as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every listed scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium. The record places that moratorium in May 2026 and marks the Bali result as Blocked (risk class). The practical conclusion is precise: national foreign ownership may reach 100%, but PMA registration for this activity in Bali is blocked under the stated provincial moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: A national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling does not turn into a Bali PMA registration right.
